title.narrative: Sustainable Economic empowerment and Development in the Nile Corridor - SEED

description.narrative: Sustainable Economic Empowerment and Development (SEED) will increase knowledge, practices and capacities of farmers, fishermen and traders in the Nile Corridor (Section between Malakal and Renk) densely populated. The project interventions targets the agricultural and market systems, where communities face a combination of recurrent flooding, drought, market disruptions and protracted insecurity that have severely undermined local food production and access. Despite fertile land and strong agricultural potential, limted accss to quality seeds, imputs and functiong markets coninues to trap households in chronic food insecurity. Project aims to strengthen resilience and food security in Upper Nile by enhancing communities understanding of ecosystems and empoering them as agents of change. It supports increased food production, diversification, and improved market access to sustain livelihoods. It will prioritize community engagement, inclusive decision-making, youth and women empowerrment as central to recovery and long-term sustainability. It will empower women and youth as agents of change. Targets: 12,960 people (7,128 women)
